knowledge:
- key_parameters: B=The number of logic regression models to consider (e.g., B = 20) ;; nleaves=The maximum number of leaves/variables allowed in the logic regression models (e.g., nleaves = 10) ;; rand=An integer seed for reproducibility ;; anneal.control=A list of control parameters for simulated annealing, generated by logreg.anneal.control() ;; coded=A logical parameter for plot() where FALSE displays original variable names instead of coded names (e.g., X1, X2) ;; obb=A logical parameter for logic.bagging indicating whether out-of-bag error should be computed ;; importance=A logical parameter for logic.bagging indicating whether variable importance should be calculated
- alternatives: The documentation mentions standard Logic Regression (Ruczinski et al., 2003) and its application to sequence analysis (Kooperberg et al., 2001), but positions logicFS as a wrapper that adds bagging and feature selection.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you want to identify complex, multi-variable Boolean interactions (e.g., SNP interactions) associated with a binary outcome (such as case-control status) and measure their importance.
- pitfalls: Running a multiple tree analysis (by changing the default ntrees) on datasets where cases are perfectly/unambiguously classified by simple logic expressions can cause numerous warnings from glm. Additionally, there is currently no internal check in predict() to ensure that the new dataset contains the same variables in the same order as the training dataset.

workflows.name: interaction_importance_logicfs
workflows.intent: Identify and measure the importance of SNP interactions using logic regression feature selection.
input: data.logicfs (matrix of categorical SNP genotypes with values 1, 2, or 3)
cl.logicfs (vector of binary class labels, e.g., 0 and 1)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and data ;; 2. Convert categorical SNP variables into binary dummy variables ;; 3. Set up simulated annealing control parameters ;; 4. Run logic regression feature selection ;; 5. Visualize interaction importance
workflows.code:
library(logicFS)
data(data.logicfs)
bin.snps <- make.snp.dummy(data.logicfs)
my.anneal <- logreg.anneal.control(start = 2, end = -2, iter = 10000)
log.out <- logicFS(bin.snps, cl.logicfs, B = 20, nleaves = 10, rand = 1234, anneal.control = my.anneal)
log.out
plot(log.out)

workflows.name: bagged_logic_regression_classification
workflows.intent: Train a bagged logic regression classifier, estimate out-of-bag error, and predict classes of new observations.
input: data.logicfs (matrix of categorical SNP genotypes with values 1, 2, or 3)
cl.logicfs (vector of binary class labels, e.g., 0 and 1)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and data ;; 2. Convert categorical SNP variables into binary dummy variables ;; 3. Set up simulated annealing control parameters ;; 4. Train a bagged logic regression model ;; 5. Inspect variable importance from the bagged model ;; 6. Predict class labels for observations and calculate misclassification rate
workflows.code:
library(logicFS)
data(data.logicfs)
bin.snps <- make.snp.dummy(data.logicfs)
my.anneal <- logreg.anneal.control(start = 2, end = -2, iter = 10000)
bag.out <- logic.bagging(bin.snps, cl.logicfs, B = 20, nleaves = 10, rand = 1234, anneal.control = my.anneal)
bag.out
bag.out$vim
cl.preds <- predict(bag.out, bin.snps)
mean(cl.preds != cl.logicfs)
